# Statement Of Architecture Work — Domain and schema — aggregates, state machines, baseline domain migration

## Assignment

What the architecture work is asked to deliver and for whom.

```json
{
  "category": "statement-of-architecture-work",
  "count": 1,
  "rows": [

      "body": {
        "acceptance_criteria": "The SPEC \u00a78 S3 gate: proptest on transitions and schema review. Property (a) \u2014 no transition leaves list.kind and archived_at contradictory, proved by board.rs::archived_implies_the_card_sits_in_an_archive_list and ::restore_off_a_non_archive_list_is_an_error. Property (b) \u2014 claim not granted twice without release or expiry, proved as tested by claim_race.rs::thirty_two_racers_get_exactly_one_grant_and_the_fence_is_monotonic, with the lease-exclusivity half recorded as the P1 package v1-s03-1. Property (c) \u2014 one pending approval per (run, gate), proved by approval_race.rs::sixteen_racers_create_exactly_one_pending_approval. Property (d) \u2014 terminal run and dense revision, proved by transitions.rs::a_terminal_run_rejects_every_transition_and_a_revision_is_dense. Tenant isolation is proved by rls_domain.rs::the_fourteen_domain_tables_isolate_runtime_owner_and_superuser. The schema review against data-arch \u00a72.3/\u00a72.4 admits the P2 package v1-s03-2. The rework's acceptance instrument is acceptance/programme/S03.toml; the closure gate is decided by an approver other than its requester.",
        "assignment": "Rework the V1 slice S03 (SPEC \u00a76, \u00a78 S3) by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: produce and publish the seven mandatory Phase A\u2013D artefacts, the charter and the delivery contract, take the project baseline with the one WBS deliverable, record the Phase-G compliance review, publish the project's expected outputs (`project-brief`, `evidence`) and the closure review, and re-close through the one gate on the P0-only gate.",
        "responsibilities": {
          "approver": "conveyor-approver",
          "architecture board": "conveyor-architecture-board",
          "programme architect": "conveyor-e2e"
        },
        "retrospective": true,
        "scope": "the baseline domain of SPEC \u00a75.3 and \u00a76: the fourteen tables of migrations/0002_domain.sql (programme, project, board, list, card_type, card, run, approval, approval_decision, governed_asset, trace_link, catalogue_entry, revision, andon_state), the may_move matrix and the run/approval/asset state machines, the store `_tx` modules with TenantId, and the catalogue_entry.kind vocabulary. Out of scope: every route and action (S04\u2013S06), the board satellites (S05), channels and delivery (S06), outlines, quality and project_request (S07), models, views and portfolio registers (S08), documents and secrets (S09), conversations (S10), procedures (S11), workflow (S13) and the capability columns (S15)."
      },
      "created_at": "2026-11-21T23:12:15.079018+00:00",
      "id": "01a20061-bd73-7a89-b08c-bd8b867eb061",

}

# Delivery Contract — Tool platform

## Commitments

The record the section derives from, or an explicit absence.

```json
{
  "category": "delivery-contract",
  "count": 1,
  "rows": [
    {
      "approval_id": "01a20277-4be1-78c6-8516-728eb4d6068b",
      "approved_at": "2026-11-22T08:55:08.219506+00:00",
      "approved_by": "01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545",
      "body": "# Delivery contract \u2014 T13 Tool platform (retrospective, 2026-11-22)\n\n**Scope.** IN: the broker tools.call; tool, toolkit, tool_binding and tool_call; effect classes read/write/destructive/spend; binding-scoped credential aliases over sealed secrets; the direct MinIO storage adapter with the tenant prefix; the coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit; V1's external actions migrated onto toolkit operations and artifacts.list onto the storage adapter; the six T13 gate proofs. OUT: catalogue actions and the estate import (T14); the agent platform gateway nonagenticai_mcp_server (D44/D59); BYO publication surface (gap ledger v1-w4a-6); live MinIO wiring (v1-p1110-1); a production tool_binding writer (v1-p111-1).\n\n**Assignment.** Project T13 \"Tool platform\", issue #76, depends on T2, spec SPEC_V2 \u00a711.1-\u00a711.10, SPEC_V2 \u00a712 T13, plan status authorised (tranche 3).\n\n**Acceptance criteria.** The \u00a712 gate, per clause:\n\na. A development job calls coding through the broker, not nonagenticai_mcp_server. *Proof:* a_bound_job_calls_coding_through_the_broker: 200; exactly one stub hit; output path /api/jobs via the registered coding destination alias.\nb. A tool_call is recorded. *Proof:* one_call_is_one_ledger_row: exactly one row for one call, tool_key coding.jobs.create, toolkit version 1, status ok, http_status 200, 64-hex sha256 input hash, latency; exactly one tool.called event.\nc. A destructive call without the tenant's configured approvals is refused. *Proof:* a_destructive_call_without_approvals_is_refused: 403 approval_required; zero destination hits; no tool_call row.\nd. Schema-invalid input is refused before the backend call. *Proof:* a_closed_schema_refuses_before_the_call: 422 tool_input_invalid with populated errors[] for an undeclared property, a pattern violation and a numeric bound; zero destination hits; a valid document returns 200 and reaches the destination.\ne. A job writes and reads a tenant-prefixed object. *Proof:* a_job_round_trips_a_tenant_prefixed_object: key starts tenant/<tenant_id>/; sha256 matches; read-back bytes match; a wrong hash is refused; head finds the object; a traversal name is refused.\nf. The compiled prompt carries no S3 key. *Proof:* the_compiled_prompt_carries_no_s3_key: compiled copilot_system@1 contains none of the access-key, secret-key or CONVEYOR_S3_ sentinels.\n\n**Responsibilities.**\n\n- **T13 delivery** \u2014 Ship the broker tools.call, the four catalogue/ledger tables, credential-alias resolution, the tenant-prefixed storage adapter and the proving tests.\n- **T2** \u2014 Supplies the run and durable-queue context; tool_binding.run_id targets a run, and \u00a712 places T13 after T2.\n- **T14** \u2014 Owns the estate import; this slice ships no catalogue actions, per the test header.\n- **Coding fleet owner** \u2014 Registers and reviews the coding destination alias; no caller-supplied URL is admitted at call time (\u00a711.3 step 5).\n- **Tenant admins** \u2014 Configure destructive-call approvals (\u00a711.4) and approve BYO toolkit publication (\u00a711.5).\n- **Platform operator** \u2014 Publishes immutable versions, runs tools.probe and retires zero-call tools (\u00a711.6, \u00a711.9).\n\n**Manifest.** The storage, tool and prompt entries are symbol references read from the tests, not independently opened file paths. No migration filename or source pin is asserted because none was read. Adds tables tool, toolkit, tool_binding, tool_call; action tools.call; event tool.called.\n\n**Retrospective.** Authored from \u00a711 and the six proving tests; no gate run is recorded in this record. # Compliance Review — Decision ladder

## Relationship

Exactly one of irrelevant, consistent, compliant, conformant, fully conformant or non-conformant.

```json

  "count": 2,

        "manifest": "acceptance/programme/T2.toml",
        "sha": "7ff27efd65146630e62d9c235458be789fb68c14"
      },
      "findings": "This retrospective Phase-G review records the compliance level non_conformant for T2 under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. It names the six findings this batch admitted, each by id and by what is missing. v1-t2-1 (P0) \u2014 a generated draft can be attached by `documents.compose` with no gate: the action accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and writes an attached, active document; the `draft.apply` gate exists only in `ladder.apply_draft` and the generated-class refusal only in `documents.update`, so the create path bypasses both. This finding blocks closure of the fourth \u00a712 clause, \"a generated draft cannot transition a card\", and therefore blocks closure of T2. v1-t2-2 \u2014 L1 never calls laya: `ladder.evaluate` records the `answer`, `confidence`, `probabilities` and `latency_ms` supplied by its caller; `laya_configs` pins model_ref, params and timeout_ms, but no T2 path issues `POST /v1/systemone`, so the recorded L1 decision is a shape, not an inference. v1-t2-3 \u2014 `refinements.publish` is ungated: the action writes the tenant's threshold, rule and fail-action override and bumps its version with `confirm = \"none\"` and no approval, although \u00a77.2 calls a refinement change a gated policy change; `decision_policies.update` is likewise ungated. v1-t2-4 \u2014 options and questions are inline free text: `ladder.evaluate` accepts an `options` array of key/label/payload objects and a free `question` string in the request, and `decision_policy` carries kind, gate, threshold, fail_policy and action but no authored question, `fire_when` or `min_confidence`, so \u00a77.2's \"options are rows, questions are rows\" is not met. v1-t2-5 \u2014 budget code spelling: \u00a77.5 records `429 budget_exceeded`, but T2 enforces no inference budget and the only budget refusal in the tree is the tool-spend `429 tool_budget_exceeded` in `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs` and `crates/actions/src/broker.rs` (#526), so the documented slug has no implementation. v1-t2-6 \u2014 a human decision cites any approved approval, not its gate: `ladder.record` calls `human_approved_gate_tx(..., None, card_id)`, so the `gate` it was given is never compared with `approval.gate`; only `ladder.apply_draft` passes `Some(DRAFT_APPLY_GATE)`, and a `gate.precheck` decision can cite an approval for a different gate on the same card. The delivered clauses are proved by named tests: `decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape`, `::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change`, `::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions` and, on the apply/update paths, `::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card`, with `ladder_human_gate.rs::a_service_principal_cannot_record_a_human_decision`, `::a_human_decision_without_an_approved_human_gate_is_refused`, `::a_pending_approval_cannot_gate_a_draft` and `::a_human_draft_apply_decision_and_approval_applies_the_draft`. The close also carried a mandatory_artefacts gap: at the 2026-11-21T19:24:46Z rework snapshot the seven Phase A\u2013D artefacts, the Statement of Architecture Work and the delivery contract were absent; this rework produces and publishes stakeholder_map, driver_goal_objective, requirements_catalog and solution_concept (Phase A), business_capability_map (Phase B), data_entity_catalog (Phase C) and technology_standards (Phase D), and records this review. No original Phase-G review existed; this one is retrospective and does not attest contemporaneous intent.\n\nDispositions at this review. v1-t2-1 is FIXED: `documents.compose` now derives the generated class from the request's attribution and stamps `meta.generated` server-side, so a caller cannot unset it, and a `card_id` on a generated draft is refused `409 draft_requires_gate`; proved at `920a1dcbfa6427b59aada92a63b6c29eb6bdcde6` by `crates/actions/tests/documents_compose_gate.rs` (4/4) with `process_step` (20/20). The P0 that blocked closure is therefore lifted and the ledger carries it resolved. v1-t2-3 (`refinements.publish` ungated) and v1-t2-6 (a human decision cites any approved approval) remain open P1 packages owned by T2 and scheduled behind this batch; v1-t2-5 is a P2 correction. Under this programme's manifest the product gate is P0-only, so the two P1s do not block closure, and they are carried as packages rather than waived.",
